mcf7.title: Breast Cancer Selectivity
mcf7.cardSummary: MCF-7 σ_i = 0.23 S/m (vs MCF-10A 0.30 S/m) lowers its EP threshold to 589 V/cm, creating a +78 V/cm window where cancer cells lyse first. TI = 1.13.
mcf7.publishedResult: MCF-7 breast cancer cells have lower cytoplasm conductivity (σ_i = 0.23 S/m) and smaller radius (R = 8.15 µm) than MCF-10A normal breast epithelium (σ_i = 0.30 S/m, R = 10 µm), per Anand 2019 Table 1. The Schwan formula applied to these values predicts E_lys(MCF-7) = 589 V/cm and E_lys(MCF-10A) = 667 V/cm, a selectivity window of +78 V/cm where the cancer cell lyses first, giving TI = 1.13. ResoPulse loads the same parameters and applies the same formula.

mcf7.step0: Resetting lab to safe baseline before loading experiment cells
mcf7.step1: Loading reference cell: MCF-10A normal breast epithelium
mcf7.step1r: MCF-10A radius R = 10 µm. Predicted E_lys = 1.0 V / (1.5 x 10 µm) = 667 V/cm.
mcf7.step1s: MCF-10A conductivity σ_i = 0.30 S/m (Anand 2019, Table 1). Sets fc and Vm roll-off frequency.
mcf7.step1v: MCF-10A threshold Vth = 1.0 V (Polevaya 1999). E_lys = Vth / (1.5 R) = 667 V/cm confirmed.
mcf7.step2: Loading target cell: MCF-7 (Anand 2019 Table 1, σ_i = 0.23 S/m, R = 8.15 µm)
mcf7.step2r: MCF-7 radius R = 8.15 µm (Anand 2019). Smaller radius alone lowers E_lys to 588 V/cm.
mcf7.step2s: MCF-7 conductivity σ_i = 0.23 S/m (0.77x MCF-10A). Lower σ_i is the primary selectivity driver.
mcf7.step2v: MCF-7 threshold Vth = 0.72 V. Combined with R = 8.15 µm: E_lys = 589 V/cm, TI = 667/589 = 1.13.
mcf7.step3: Setting medium: EP buffer (σ_e = 0.14 S/m), standard low-conductivity EP medium
mcf7.step4: Setting waveform: pulsed IRE, single-pulse protocol (N=1) to match Anand 2019's bare Schwan prediction (no electrosensitization)
mcf7.step5: Setting frequency: 10 kHz (quasi-DC, well below fc for both cell types)
mcf7.step6: Setting field: 620 V/cm, inside the selectivity window (above MCF-7 E_lys = 589, below MCF-10A = 667)
mcf7.step7: TI confirmed: MCF-7 disrupting (DR = 1.0), MCF-10A intact. Selectivity window = +78 V/cm.
mcf7.resultAgreement: The Schwan model correctly predicts that MCF-7's lower conductivity (0.23 vs 0.30 S/m) and smaller radius (8.15 vs 10 µm) reduce its lysis field to 589 V/cm, placing it below the MCF-10A threshold of 667 V/cm. The selectivity window and TI = 1.13 match the values reported by Anand et al. (2019).

ccmv.title: Viral Capsid Resonance
ccmv.cardSummary: CCMV capsid lowest acoustic mode at f_res ≈ 21 GHz (l=2 H mode, atomistic; Dykeman & Sankey 2010 Table V). Co-incubated mammalian cells unaffected: Schwan Vm collapses at GHz (f/fc > 20,000 in any standard buffer). TI greater than 99.
ccmv.publishedResult: CCMV plant virus capsid (R = 14 nm) has a predicted lowest acoustic mode at ≈ 21 GHz (l=2 H-symmetry quadrupolar mode, 0.71 cm⁻¹) from atomistic normal-mode calculation (Dykeman & Sankey, Phys. Rev. E 81:021918, 2010, Table V). Continuum elastic theory (Murray & Saviot 2007) gives ≈ 17 GHz for the same mode. The breathing mode (A symmetry) is higher at ≈ 36 GHz. The selectivity mechanism — Schwan Vm collapse for mammalian cells at GHz frequencies — is rigorous physics regardless of which specific mode is excited. Note: f_res, Q, and E_thr are model parameters; no direct experimental disruption measurement for CCMV at GHz exists in the literature.
ccmv.publishedMetric: CCMV lowest mode ≈ 21 GHz (atomistic, Dykeman 2010); selectivity via mammalian Schwan Vm collapse

ccmv.step0: Resetting lab to safe baseline before loading experiment cells
ccmv.step1: Loading reference cell: hepatocyte (mammalian, R = 10 µm)
ccmv.step1r: Hepatocyte radius: R = 10 µm. fc ≈ 0.45 MHz at EP buffer (≈ 1 MHz at saline). At 21 GHz (>40,000x above fc at EP buffer), Schwan Vm approaches zero.
ccmv.step2: Loading target cell: CCMV plant virus capsid (R = 14 nm)
ccmv.step2f: CCMV resonant frequency: f_res ≈ 21 GHz (lowest H mode, l=2 quadrupolar, from Dykeman & Sankey 2010 atomistic normal-mode calculation, Table V). Range across modes and methods: 17–36 GHz. This is a model prediction, not a direct experimental measurement.
ccmv.step2q: CCMV quality factor: Q ≈ 4 from solvent damping in water (Murray & Saviot 2007 lifetime; Dykeman 2010 Table VI). Slightly underdamped — broader resonance than vacuum-elastic models would predict.
ccmv.step4: Setting frequency: 21 GHz (21,000,000 kHz), the predicted lowest CCMV capsid resonant mode
ccmv.step5: Setting field: 500 V/cm (model acoustic disruption threshold parameter)
ccmv.step6: Resonance chart: CCMV DR ≥ 1 (capsid at the disruption threshold), hepatocyte DR near zero (Vm collapsed)
ccmv.resultAgreement: The acoustic resonance model shows selective CCMV capsid disruption at the lowest predicted mode f_res ≈ 21 GHz (Dykeman & Sankey 2010 atomistic model). At this frequency, hepatocyte Schwan Vm collapses to near zero (f/fc > 20,000 in any standard buffer), producing TI > 99. The selectivity mechanism — Schwan Vm collapse for large cells at GHz — is the physically rigorous result. The specific f_res, Q, and E_thr values are model predictions; treat this scenario as a demonstration of resonance selectivity rather than a reproduction of a single experimental dataset.
